CHENNAI BOXING World Boxing U-19 Championships: Dominant Aditya eases into gold medal bout against Magomedov of Russia Aditya became the second Indian boxer to make it to the finals of the 2026 World Boxing U-19 Championships in Budva, Montenegro, as he defeated Nihat Gasimov of Azerbaijan in the men’s 55kg semifinals on Sunday evening. Aditya, the Asian U-19 silver medallist, was dominant through the three rounds to bag a 5:0 verdict from the judges and will now face Islam Magomedov of Russia in the gold meda bout. Megha Sheokand had earlier clinched the final spot in the women’s 80kg category with a RSC win over Meerim Chynybekova of Kyrgyzstan in the semifinals. India will also come home with two bronze medals. On Sunday evening, Harshika’s gallant fight against USA’s Lauryn Elmore was not enough as she ended on the wrong side of the 3:2 verdict in the women’s 65kg semifinals. Earlier, Prachi Tokas had bagged a bronze medal in the women’s 80+kg category after losing her semifinal bout. - Team Sportstar MOTORSPORT John Abraham joins Indian Superbike League as Strategic Advisor center Actor-entrepreneur John Abraham has joined Indian Superbike League (ISBL) as its Strategic Advisor. Indian Superbike League Indian Superbike League https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/38hwo1/article71627195.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/John%20Abraham%20joins%20Indian%20Superbike%20League%20as%20Strategic%20Advisor.png Indian Superbike League Actor-entrepreneur John Abraham has joined Indian Superbike League (ISBL) as its Strategic Advisor. Sanctioned by the Federation of Motor Sports Clubs of India (FMSCI), ISBL will operate as a franchise-based championship featuring two Pro categories, Amateur, Female Riders and Rookie classes. ISBL aims to create a structured competitive environment for riders while opening opportunities across teams, technical personnel, brands, creators and the wider motorsport ecosystem. Speaking about his association with ISBL, Abraham said, “Motorcycles have always been a deeply personal passion. Being a sports team owner has also taught me what it takes to turn belief into sustained commitment. ISBL brings those two parts of my life together. I want to help young Indian riders get the opportunities they deserve and share the thrill of motorcycle racing with a whole new generation of fans. It’s time to Get India Racing.” Further details on teams, riders, race formats and venues will be announced in due course. - Team Sportstar SQUASH Agastya Bansal, Kriya Saravanan create upsets in Sub-Junior & Junior National squash Agastya Bansal of Maharashtra stunned Karnataka 3/4 seed Rahul Sanjay Balakrishnan 11-4, 11-1, 7-11, 11-9 in the U-19 boys pre-quarterfinals of the Sub-Junior & Junior National Squash Championship in Jaipur on Monday. In girls’ U-19, Tamil Nadu’s Kriya Saravanan beat 5/8 seed Aishni Pathak of Madhya Pradesh 11-4, 3-11, 8-11, 11-7, 11-4 to advance to the quarterfinals. Among other upsets in pre-quarters, Dhairya Gogia of Rajasthan took out state-mate and second seed Fareed Andrabi 11-8, 7-11, 11-6, 6-11, 16-14 in boys’ U-15 and Pradeepsingh Rathore ousted Karnataka state-mate and 5/8 seed Aryaman Singh 11-4, 12-10, 2-11, 8-11, 14-12 in boys’ U-17. - Team Sportstar TABLE TENNIS WTT Youth Contender Chennai: Sakshya Santhosh stuns top seed Sananda Srijith; Sayanika Maji, Himon Mondal storm into semis Third seed Sakshya Santhosh knocked out top seed Sananda Srijith 11-7, 9-11, 11-1, 11-4 in the U11 girls’ singles quarterfinals of the WTT Youth Contender Chennai 2026, presented by Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu, at the Tamil Nadu Physical Education and Sports University on Monday. The four-day tournament, being held from October 23 to 26, features 12 categories from U11 to U19. Sakshya will now face second seed Aadya Baheti in the semifinals, while ninth seed Kritika Saibo, who blanked fifth seed Nandhana Bandi, meets seventh seed Anika Maheshwari. In the U19 girls’ singles, 11th seed Sayanika Maji blanked fifth seed Naisha Rewaskar 11-8, 11-7, 11-7 in the pre-quarterfinals before getting the better of third seed Prisha Goel 11-0, 8-11, 11-3, 11-5. She will now face 12th seed Swara Karmarkar, who dropped just one game all day and beat 27th seed Aarushi Nandi 11-3, 4-11, 11-4, 11-2. Top seed Divyanshi Bhowmick edged seventh seed Jennifer Varghese 12-10, 11-7, 10-12, 12-10 to set up a quarterfinal against sixth seed Ananya Muralidharan, while USA’s Satya Aspathi, the second seed, came from two games down to beat 13th seed Anvi Gupte and will meet fourth seed Hansini Mathan. The 13-year-old Himon Mondal, seeded 20th, stunned fifth seed Koh Wei Yeow of Malaysia 11-3, 11-9, 9-11, 11-4 and then ended the run of 49th seed Rounak Sarkar 11-9, 12-10, 11-5 to reach the U15 boys’ semifinals. Rounak had earlier packed off fourth seed Vivaan Dave. Himon will now face second seed Vatsal Duklan, who blanked seventh seed Prateek Tulsani 11-8, 11-6, 11-4. Third seed Sanjey Arwindh also fell, losing to 34th seed Shriram Kiran 10-12, 11-8, 11-9, 7-11, 11-6. Shriram meets 22nd seed Sathyanarayanan Karmeghakannan in the quarterfinals, while top seed Aditya Das takes on sixth seed Rishaan Chattopadhayay. In the U19 boys’ singles, 15th seed Sahil Rawat blanked third seed Sudhanshu Maini 11-8, 11-8, 11-6 to set up a quarterfinal clash against 10th seed Arjav Gupta, who got the better of sixth seed Ahmed Korani of Qatar. Seventh seed Kumar Harshit came from 1-2 down to knock out fourth seed Nikkhil Mannath 11-9, 12-14, 6-11, 11-8, 11-4 and will meet 16th seed Atharva Nawarange. Forty-third seed Nikunj Attri edged 21st seed Ronald Sarkar 11-9, 9-11, 10-12, 11-9, 12-10 to earn a quarterfinal against top seed Abhinandh Pradhivadhi, while second seed Priyanuj Bhattacharyya, who outlasted ninth seed Punit Biswas in five games, meets fifth seed Ritvik Gupta. In the U15 girls’ singles, 34th seed Shreya Dhar blanked fifth seed Janvi Garg 11-3, 11-6, 11-6 and will face second seed Sreejani Chakraborty, while 40th seed Ranjini Saha got the better of eighth seed Subhomita Basak in four games to meet top seed Ahona Ray. Tenth seed Advika Agrawal edged fourth seed Sri Saanvi Kamarapu 8-11, 11-3, 3-11, 11-8, 12-10 and will play the 12-year-old Ishani Gogoi, seeded 11th, who knocked out seventh seed Divija Paul. In the U11 boys’ singles, top seed Sharvil Karambelkar eased past 11th seed Ashank Dalvi 11-5, 11-1, 11-7 to set up a semifinal against third seed Rehansh Singhvi, who beat fourth seed Ishaan Colaso. Second seed Pranit Agrawal will meet 15th seed Arnav Mithun. - Team Sportstar SWIMMING Kushagra Rawat, Sajan Prakash clinch gold at Short Course Swimming Championship Delhi’s Kushagra Rawat clinched the gold medal in the men’s 1500m freestyle event at the inaugural Short Course Senior National Aquatic Championships in Ahmedabad on Monday. The 26-year-old clocked 15 minutes 17.46 seconds to finish on top ahead of Sharan S of Karnataka (15:17.86). Atharvraj Patil (15:45.26) of Services Sports Control Board was a distant third. Seasoned swimmer Sajan Prakash, representing Police, won the men’s 50m butterfly in 23.19 seconds. Kerala’s Tanish George Matthew (23.52 seconds) clinched the silver medal, while Maharashtra’s Mihir Ambre (23.80 seconds) bagged the bronze. Maharashtra’s Advait Page won the men’s 400m medley in 4 minutes 24.76 seconds, with Karnataka’s Shivank Vishwanath (4:26.58) and Telangana’s Dhulipudi Varshith (4:29.82) also finishing on the podium. Tvisha Nikhil Dixit took the top honours in the women’s 400m medley with a time of 4 minutes 59.27 seconds, with Shreenithi Natesan (5:02.92) and Sanithi Mukherjee (5:04.42) finishing second and third respectively. - PTI
